newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BankWest sees profit below forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BankWest sees profit below forecast.

text.p: Bank of Western Australia Ltd said on Thursday that its net profit in the year ending February 28, 1997, was likely to be five percent below the prospectus forecast of A$100.2 million.
The bank, which is 51 percent-owned by Bank of Scotland, said it still expected the total dividend for the year to be in line with the prospectus forecast.
"The prospectus set out the key assumptions on which the forecast was based and the sensitivity of movements in housing loan margins," BankWest said.

"Having reviewed the bank's position in the light of recent falls in interest rates and increased competitive pressure, the directors are now of the view that based on results to the end of January theprofit for the year ending February 28 1997 is likely to be around five percent less than the prospectus forecast," the bank said.
Audited annual results will be issued on April 23.
BankWest, which was formerly owned by the state government of Western Australia, also made a prospectus forecast of a fully-franked 1996/97 dividend of 16.5 cents per share.
Chairman Ian Mackenzie said the bank's profits were being adversely affected by lower rates and reduced margins, even though market share was growing and it had strong lending volumes.
"The full effect of recent interest rate reductions will be felt in the coming year and will have a negative impact on the bank's profit," the bank said in a statement.
